entradas.text: I was walking to my office, since today was the day to edit and make the final changes for the proposal to change the Constitution of Sordland.
Not long after, Petr, Lucian and Nia arrived.
“Greetings.”
entradas.menu: “Greetings.”

entradas.text: “Finally!”
entradas.menu: “Finally!”

entradas.text: I walked in the marble corridors of the Palace, thinking about the huge decisions I was going to take.
At the entrance to my office, my secretary Livia greeted me.
"Good morning, Mr. President."
"Good morning! Time to finally get this proposal going."
The reform committee finally bore tangible results and the draft of the changes were about to be presented to me.
"Good morning, Mr. President."
“Good morning, Livia.”
entradas.menu: “Good morning, Livia.”

entradas.text: "How are you today?"
entradas.menu: "How are you today?"

entradas.text: "Fine, thank you."
"More importantly, how are you, sir?"
"How are you today, sir?"
“I'm about to make stressful decisions. So, not feeling that great.”
entradas.menu: “I'm about to make stressful decisions. So, not feeling that great.”

entradas.text: “I'm perfectly fine."
entradas.menu: “I'm perfectly fine."

entradas.text: “I feel better now that I've seen you, Livia."
entradas.menu: “I feel better now that I've seen you, Livia."

entradas.text: She averted her eyes away from me and smiled.
"Good to hear."
"Sorry to hear."
"Thank you, Mr. President."
“You'll find out with the rest of Sordland, sweetheart."
entradas.menu: “You'll find out with the rest of Sordland, sweetheart."

entradas.text: “I'll take that into consideration."
entradas.menu: “I'll take that into consideration."

entradas.text: "Nothing's been decided yet."
entradas.menu: "Nothing's been decided yet."

entradas.text: “That's none of your business, Livia."
entradas.menu: “That's none of your business, Livia."

entradas.text: Livia left to hang up my coat. I entered my office and sat down.
“Good morning everybody.”
entradas.menu: “Good morning everybody.”

entradas.text: Petr placed the draft in front of me.
"After your modifications, we will be starting the process."
After placing the committee's report and my own notes in front of me, I buried myself in the papers.
"I have suggested to bring some limitations to decrees regarding their applicability. While we keep them, we should try to make sure that they will only be used in emergency situations."
"Regardless of him, I see no problem with having a special title for great heroes."
entradas.menu: "Regardless of him, I see no problem with having a special title for great heroes."

entradas.text: "It's just a title, Mrs. Morgna."
entradas.menu: "It's just a title, Mrs. Morgna."

entradas.text: "Mr. President. Unless you wish to be like Colonel Soll after all."

"We could start talking about Section 3. This is about the impeachment process of the President. Currently, in cases of high treason and breaking the Constitution, the Supreme Court may impeach and try the President."
"After pushing aggressive changes, I may need the same immunity."
entradas.menu: "After pushing aggressive changes, I may need the same immunity."

entradas.text: "If our own democracy is the reason of our downfall, we will have to accept it."
entradas.menu: "If our own democracy is the reason of our downfall, we will have to accept it."

entradas.text: "It's not unfair that former Presidents get some special treatment."
entradas.menu: "It's not unfair that former Presidents get some special treatment."

entradas.text: "It is a matter of both when we have the Communist Party and the Workers Party of Bludia getting more than five percent vote in the last elections."
"Well, regardless of what Mr. Rayne decides, we will need to work together to push this agenda."
"Most reformists want the impeachment to be initiated by the Assembly. They think they do not have any power over potential rogue presidents that would abuse their power."
"Don't forget that the Communist Party and the Workers Party of Bludia both had close to ten percent vote in the last election."
"You're right. Even after Soll's resignation, we still have three parties in the Assembly. Even Mr. Kibener's NFP was barely elected."
"The Assembly should have oversight over the President, it is the most democratic institution."
entradas.menu: "The Assembly should have oversight over the President."

entradas.text: "Not sure if it is correct to chastise the President this much though."
entradas.menu: "Not sure if it is correct to chastise the President this much though."

entradas.text: "I'm sorry, Mr. President?"
"That would be enough to hold him accountable for his actions but why would you want to keep such a title, Mr. President?"
"The reformists would be completely behind that."
"I agree. Even after Soll's resignation, we still have three parties in the Assembly. Even Mr. Kibener's NFP is barely elected."
"Do you want to protect Tarquin Soll, Mr. President?"
"Yes, he is a hero for Sordland."
entradas.menu: "Yes, he is a hero for Sordland."

entradas.text: "This law is particularly dangerous for you in this case. We will be going against the Old Guard, and if we prove to be successful in the Assembly..."
"Decreasing the threshold might mean opening their way into the Assembly."
"We could even remove impeachment altogether, I can get total immunity."
entradas.menu: "We could even remove impeachment altogether."

entradas.text: "I agree, we should abolish this position."
entradas.menu: "I agree, we should abolish this position."

entradas.text: "You would be opening their way into the parliament in the future if you were to decrease the threshold. It is important that you realize this."
"We should define a more refined impeachment process."
entradas.menu: "We should define a better impeachment process."

entradas.text: "I think this is a national matter, Mr. Rayne. Not a partisan one."
"No, I think we should respect this law."
entradas.menu: "No, I think we should respect this law."

entradas.text: "We could keep the title but take away the immunity clause."
entradas.menu: "We could keep the title but take away the immunity clause."

entradas.text: "Every President should gain that title after their term."
entradas.menu: "Every President should gain that title after their term."

entradas.text: "Maybe the reforms are not a great idea after all."
entradas.menu: "Maybe reforms are not a great idea after all."

entradas.text: "Many Sordish citizens feel they're not represented in the Assembly. This is a matter of representative democracy in Sordland."
"What if we don't succeed? The Court can have me impeached for this."
entradas.menu: "What if we don't succeed? The Court can have me impeached for this."

entradas.text: "...They will be looking for anything they can declare unconstitutional to tackle you. All they need is the Supreme Court to impeach you."
"We must get rid of this senseless law that protects him. He should be able to face justice for the atrocities that had taken place during his rule."
"Of course that would also mean that USP might lose its majority in the Assembly, sir."

"That's why only Tarquin Soll has that title. He gave it to himself right after his military coup. This law is basically made to save the Colonel and it has a symbolic importance for Sordland because of it."

"According to the Constitution, the Member of Honor not only has legal immunity but the state also covers most of their expenses as well as providing security at all times. It can only be given to someone by an absolute majority vote in the Assembly and the approval of the President."
"Mr. Ricter and his PFJP definitely wants to see change on this topic. They find our 10% threshold to be antidemocratic. Which is something I also agree with."

"And the last one is the question about Soll's legacy. Basically his *Member of Honor* law. It gave him absolute immunity even when he's retired. He is a permanent member of the Assembly as well, but luckily he doesn't really attend anymore."
"I agree with you, Mr. President."
"This is out of the question."
entradas.menu: "This is out of the question."

entradas.text: "I may need to think a bit longer about this."
entradas.menu: "I may need to think a bit longer about this."

entradas.text: "While I do not have strong opinions about this point, these reforms are vital for the future of our democracy, Mr. President."
"But it would be tougher to persuade the judges with this. Mrs. Edmonds may not want to cooperate with you if they believe you're going to get rid of them afterwards."
"Yes, they are already trying to hit you since they are aware about the current wind of change. But we aim to cooperate with some of the judges to make sure that doesn't happen."
"Yes, we will be collaboratively working on the specifics."
"That is a better strategy. We'll need to sway some of their members to succeed after all."
"Hell yes, we should."
"That might be the best thing to do for now. If we agitate the Court further, we might lose our chances with Mrs. Edmonds as well."
"Exactly."
"We should respect their immunity."
entradas.menu: "We should respect their immunity."

entradas.text: "They should be able to be impeached. Why do I get to be impeached but not them?"
entradas.menu: "They should be able to be impeached. Why do I get to be impeached but not them?"

entradas.text: "We should crush the Old Guards to clear ways for further reforms in Sordland."
entradas.menu: "We should crush the Old Guards to clear ways for further reforms."

entradas.text: "Maybe we shouldn't make the Supreme Court our enemies just yet. Let's keep the reforms light."
entradas.menu: "Maybe we shouldn't make the Supreme Court our enemies just yet."

entradas.text: "We can't allow communists to enter the Assembly and endanger Sordland."
entradas.menu: "We can't allow communists to enter the Assembly."

entradas.text: "I don't think that's a wise idea to include in the reforms."
"We can't just give away our majority like that."
entradas.menu: "We can't just give away our majority like that."

entradas.text: "We will make sure the Old Guards won't control the Court any longer, Mr. President."
"Well, they need absolute immunity in theory. But look at what reality got us? We've got to deal with the most corrupt Chief Justice in the world, with no chance to deal with him!"
"Section 6. This is about the presidential decrees. Reformists demand more limitations to the President's executive powers. Mr. Ricter has demanded them to be completely removed."
"Uhm. The next one..."
"Don't worry. With these reforms, we will be even more popular."
entradas.menu: "Don't worry. With these reforms, we will be even more popular."

entradas.text: "We'll work with the reformists to limit the use of decrees."
entradas.menu: "We'll work with the reformists to limit the use of decrees."

entradas.text: "But the high threshold is the reason why Sordish politics has become isolated to this degree."
entradas.menu: "But the high threshold is the reason why Sordish politics has become so isolated."

entradas.text: "While I agree that the current court members are *problematic*, this is no way to resolve it. The law is supposed to ensure the judiciary's independence by giving legal protection so they can't be pressured."
"We should definitely work to decrease the threshold for better representation in our democracy."
entradas.menu: "We should definitely work to decrease the threshold for better representation."

entradas.text: "I do not support taking away their power for yourself, Mr. President. The judiciary must be independent and long-lasting."
"Section 4."
"It's the question about the immunity of the Judges. While the Anti-Old Guard sentiment is increasing, there are talks that taking away their immunity would give us authority over judiciary."
"Now I'll move unto the 8th Section. We are reaching the end."
"Do you think it would really hurt the party?"
entradas.menu: "Do you think it would really hurt the party?"

entradas.text: "Even Soll knew he had to leave, but we will leave it to the President to decide."
"This is regarding the appointment of ministers. Currently, the President is free to appoint anyone from the members of the Assembly. Nobody else is involved with the process."
"I will take my time and seriously consider the options before settling on one."
entradas.menu: "I will take my time and seriously consider the options before settling on one."

entradas.text: "Yes, he did. But it took a long time."
entradas.menu: "Yes, he did. But it took a long time."

entradas.text: "Some reformists suggested that the Assembly should nominate the ministers before the President approves them."
"There is definitely a demand to involve the Assembly in the process."
"It could be destabilising."
"I agree. People should be able to elect the same person if they want to."
entradas.menu: "I agree. People should be able to elect the same person if they want to."

entradas.text: "The fifth section is about our infamous electoral threshold. Most reformists want to lower the threshold as much as possible."
"I don't think presidential decrees need any reforms."
entradas.menu: "I don't think presidential decrees need any reforms."

entradas.text: "Hey, if people keep electing one person, that means they really are content. The masses are scared of change."
"We can't allow somebody like Soll holding unto his seat for two decades again. We should establish limits."
"I agree. We should involve the Assembly more in the process."
entradas.menu: "I agree. We should involve the Assembly more in the process."

entradas.text: "We could introduce a confidence vote."
entradas.menu: "We could introduce a confidence vote."

entradas.text: "They want us to include previously non-existing term limits."
"I think that's going a bit too far."
entradas.menu: "That's going a bit too far."

entradas.text: "Yes. Tarquin Soll governed for twenty years. It seems his magic is slowly vanishing from the minds of the people, for they believe term limits are necessary."
"I hope it works out, Mr. President."
"I agree, we could keep that in."
"I know it is a delicate matter, sir. But you still have time to think about these."
"I agree. We can't allow somebody like Soll holding unto his seat for two decades again."
"We could also make it dependent on an enabling act from the Assembly. Sure, it would make the whole process longer but as long as we have a majority, nothing really changes."
"Me neither. I think it's important that the President can act quickly on matters of national importance."
"That was my suggestion as well."
"Uh-oh."
entradas.menu: "Uh-oh."

entradas.text: "I don't aim to leave any time soon. We keep the unlimited terms."
entradas.menu: "I don't aim to leave any time soon. We keep the unlimited terms."

entradas.text: "Term limits are necessary."
entradas.menu: "Term limits are necessary."

entradas.text: "Term Limits?"
entradas.menu: "Term Limits?"

entradas.text: "Maybe. But Mr. Ricter doesn't think so."
"Yes, but this is a delicate matter. The party, and I mean, not even Albin wants us to change the threshold. They think that... this would destroy our party in the long term."
"Next one is Section 7. Term limits."
"Mr. Clavin and our party's reformist wing has no problems with the current law. I'm sure PFJP can be persuaded too."
"Not wrong. The ten percent threshold is what that allowed us to control half of the Assembly with around one third of the majority in the elections."
"I'm sure the reformists would completely support that."
"Of course, according to the ratio of the party's in government. In our case, it's only us."
"Frens will probably demand that we remove them completely. But he forgets that Sordland is a Presidential Republic."
Lucian continued with the next section.
"If the entire package is to their liking, I don't think Frens will resist his own. He wouldn't say no to such major changes just because of a few small details."
"Sure. You'll have a long time before we start writing the final proposal together."
“Let's start.”
entradas.menu: “Let's start.”

entradas.text: “Can we go over each of the points that are in discussion for the draft?”
entradas.menu: “Can we go over each of the points that are in discussion for the draft?”

entradas.text: "Well, apart from the first two sections of decreasing the Supreme Court's authority and limiting the presidential vetoes... Nothing else has been agreed on unanimously."
“Let's start working on the draft.”
entradas.menu: “Let's start working on the draft.”

entradas.text: “I thank you all for your input.”
entradas.menu: “I thank you all for your input.”

entradas.text: After placing the committee's report and my own notes in front of me, I buried myself in the papers.
She paused before taking my coat. It looked like she had something on her mind.
"Mr. Rayne -- can you give me a hint about your reform plans? If you ask me, taking away the judges' immunity is long overdue, but it might anger a lot of people in these halls..."
"Understood. I'll take your coat now."
"I hope you'll keep me informed. I'll take your coat now."
